claims_disputed.claim: Viverra efficiently generates C code together with verified assertions on diverse tasks
claims_disputed.reason: Table 1 is one GPT-5.1 run on 18 textbook tasks. Verification takes 2077.6s on sudoku, 981.0s on connect4, and 879.3s on knapsack (mean 316.4±542.7s). base_addition falsifies 14 of 23 assertions. 'Verified' is k=5, not task correctness.

claims_disputed.claim: Every verified property is sound within the loop-unwind bound, and conditional facts are sound under recorded assumptions
claims_disputed.reason: Theorem 1 covers VerifyAll on the program it is given. Algorithm 1 verifies P+_k after BoundReduce, which rewrites loop-bound constants, then EmbedFacts writes the comments onto original P0. Soundness is not shown for the program the developer reads.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: Fig. 3 is higher accuracy on 8 of 10 questions, but §5.3 says each question was written to match one verified assertion, the control is bare code rather than an unverified comment, and the text calls 100% vs 40% and 96s vs 82s significant with no test. That does not isolate verification as the thing that helps a reader.

missed_issues: Algorithm 1 line 6 has the LLM tighten compile-time loop bounds so every loop iterates at most k=5, and line 10 embeds facts proved on that reduced program into the original P0. A comment can describe a program the user is not looking at.
The user study shows only assumption-free facts (§5.3). Conditional facts, which are the compositional half of the method, are never shown to a reader.

Prompts for elicitation, synthesis, annotation, and fact translation are printed in Appendix C. The review's closed-artifact note is right about code and the survey files, and wrong that the prompts are absent.

§5.3 uses 'significantly' for the connected-components item (100% vs 40%, 96s vs 82s). No test, interval, or distinct-worker count is reported; the abstract's 'more than 400 participants' is at least 400 HIT completions.
note: The review is right about the title, the single model, the crowdworker quiz, and that P35 and P42 are not shown to work. It over-calls P41 as supports: the quiz can be passed by reading a comment that was written to contain the answer, which is not a comprehension safeguard winning against a real alternative. It under-calls the soundness claim by treating Theorem 1 as applying to the delivered program; bound reduction sits between the proof and the comment. Broadcom co-affiliation without a Broadcom product is low, matching the review. Blind rigor is 2 because the headline human result does not survive its own instrument. Nothing here justifies a C model checker beside Java services.
